chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about 'Subhanallah', and he said: 'Exaltation to Allah'.

key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: Exaltation to Allah / Glory be to Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Subhanallah' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise terms, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines 'Subhanallah' as 'anafah', denoting Allah’s inherent exaltation and freedom from any defect or likeness. This brief definition underscores the Shia theological emphasis on tanzih (divine transcendence), affirming that God is free from corporeality and human attributes, a key concept in the chapter on the Negation of Corporeality.
